# @arki/payments-native

> RevenueCat in-app purchases for React Native apps: configure, load the pro offering, purchase and restore, with failures returned as values.

## Import paths

<!-- llms:start -->
- `@arki/payments-native`: `OfferingsUnavailable`, `PurchaseFailed`, `RestoreFailed`, `configureRevenueCat`, `getProOffering`, `purchasePackage`, `restorePurchases`; types `ConfigureRevenueCatParams`, `CustomerInfo`, `PurchaseOutcome`, `PurchasesOffering`, `PurchasesPackage`.
<!-- llms:end -->

## Start here

- [Agent guide](docs/agent-guide.md): the model, the task map, the rules, the errors. Read it first.
- [Verify](docs/agent-guide.md#verify): the commands to run after a change.
- [README](README.md): the quick start, runtimes and observability.

## By task
- [Buy a package](docs/agent-guide.md#buy-a-package)
- [Restore purchases](docs/agent-guide.md#restore-purchases)
- [Show a placeholder before the offering exists](docs/agent-guide.md#show-a-placeholder-before-the-offering-exists)

## Rules that bite
- This package is the purchase rail only. It does not read entitlements. Ask your own backend whether the user is Pro.
- `appUserId` must be the id your backend signs users in with, or the webhook cannot find the user.
- A failure is a returned value. Check it with `isFailure`. A cancelled purchase is `{ status: 'cancelled' }`, not a failure.
- `configureRevenueCat` is the only call that can throw. Call it once at app start.
- Match on the failure `code`, never on the message.
